items.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] This is from Phil Woods, and I was able to speak with him... [INTERVIEWEE] So I think what Phil was saying there was if you want to be a musician it has to call you...

ctx.x: I have a — speaking of previous interviews, I want to read something from two individuals and just get your reaction to it. This is from Phil Woods, and I was able to speak with him, probably — I’ve lost track — fifteen years or so. And I asked him about advice for young jazz men. And he said, “I think jazz is only for those that have no choice. I think if you’re a young man and you’re entertaining thoughts of becoming a brain surgeon or a jazz tenor man, I’d go with the brain surgery. If you’ve got two burning…

Well that’s very good advice, really. I think to be — if you just look at it you know you can start thinking pretty gloomy things about even being a music major let alone being a jazz musician. But the thing is that if you take what you do to the highest possible level and if you are successful being a really fine player, people recognize that and they will you know pay for you to play. But it’s really tough, I mean some of the jazz guys going to New York nowadays, it’s not $15 they’re playing for but it’s not…
If you had a grandchild who wanted to do it, what would you say to them?
